summary:
We developed BlueTrend, an interactive WebGIS decision-support platform that monitors and protects Southeast Asia’s seagrass ecosystems using 22 years of NASA Earth Observation data (2003–2024).
Seagrass meadows are vital Blue Carbon sinks, yet they face severe degradation from ocean warming and land-based sediment runoff, while conservation managers lack localized, actionable risk data. BlueTrend solves this by integrating 21,221 seagrass polygons and 14 HydroBASINS watersheds with four NASA datasets—MODIS Sea Surface Temperature (SST), Water Turbidity (Kd490), GPM IMERG Precipitation, and AIRS CO₂. Using non-parametric Mann-Kendall and Sen’s Slope trend analysis alongside 2018–2024 spatial stress sampling, the platform classifies the top 350 major meadows into High, Medium, and Low Risk, forecasts 3-year trends, and generates context-aware conservation recommendations with one-click CSV reports.
This matters because it bridges complex satellite science with immediate coastal policy, empowering Marine Protected Area managers to prioritize restoration and safeguard Southeast Asia’s Blue Carbon.
details:
• How It Works: BlueTrend is a WebGIS platform integrating 21,221 seagrass polygons and 14 HydroBASINS watersheds with 22 years (2003–2024) of NASA Earth Observation data (MODIS SST, Kd490 turbidity, GPM IMERG rainfall, and AIRS CO₂). Using non-parametric Mann-Kendall and Sen’s Slope trend tests alongside 2018–2024 spatial stress sampling, it classifies the top 350 meadows into High (41%), Medium (37%), and Low Risk (22%), forecasts 3-year trends, and generates region-specific conservation advice with one-click CSV reports.
  • Benefits & Impact: Translates complex satellite datasets into an actionable dashboard, helping Marine Protected Area (MPA) managers pinpoint dual thermal-sediment hotspots, allocate restoration budgets efficiently, and safeguard Southeast Asia’s Blue Carbon sinks.
  • Tools & Tech Stack: NASA Giovanni & AppEEARS portals; Python (geopandas, xarray, rasterio, pymannkendall, pandas) and QGIS (EPSG:4326 GeoJSON) for geospatial processing; HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Leaflet.js, and Chart.js for the WebGIS interface.
  • Innovation & Considerations: Unlike ocean-only tools, BlueTrend links inland watersheds and rainfall to coastal turbidity (land-to-sea stress). We chose non-parametric statistics to handle El Niño seasonality and designed a species-agnostic spatial model to overcome missing ground-truth species labels in global datasets.
